newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso closes sharply weaker on long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso closes sharply weaker on long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed sharply weaker on Thursday under pressure from rebounding U.S. long bond rates, traders said.
"Many dealers bought dollars on fears that long bond rates would gain more on Friday," a trader said.
The 24-hour and benchmark 48-hour spot peso closed 2.9 and 3.5 centavos weaker at 7.5990/7.6040 and 7.6100/7.6150 per dollar, respectively.

U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yields increased to 7.16 percent following the release of lower-than-expected weekly jobless claims figures which triggered fears that the U.S. economy may be overheating and thus lead to primary rate hikes.
